The City of Pasadena is dedicated to delivering exemplary municipal services, responsive to
  our entire community and consistent

  Council Meetings. Assistive Listening headphones and neckloops can be checked out at the desk of the
  Sergeant-at-Arms, located inside the City Council Chambers. To request meeting materials in alternative
  formats or other disability-related modifications or accommodations necessary to facilitate meeting
  participation, please contact the City Clerk’s Office as soon as possible at (626) 744-4124 or

9:07 p.m.  Allison Henry, Chair of the Pasadena Rental Housing Board,
  provided information on the Board's activities such as sen/ing in a
  quasi-judicial manner, hearing appeals, utilizing ad hoc committees,
  and reviewing median rent and eviction data. Helen Morales, Rent
  Stabilization Director, reported on successfully working with Loyola
  Center as part of a Conflict Resolution effort to resolve conflicts
  between landlords and tenants.

  Councilmember Cole emphasized the importance of performance
  measures and cost controls, and expressed support for robust
  training for Pasadena Rental Housing Board Members, as well as all
  commissioners, to increase the effectiveness of all City boards and
  commissions. He advocated for the staff report to acknowledge the
  setbacks and obstacles faced by the Board and Rent Stabilization
  Department.

  Councilmember Lyon echoed similar sentiments, noting that the
  report should reflect the economic diversity throughout the City and
  the economic critique for small-time housing providers.

  In response to Councilmember Masuda's inquiry regarding the pay
  for Pasadena Rental Housing Board Members, Rent Stabilization
  Director Morales reported that the Board Members are paid 2.5 times
  the Pasadena minimum wage at $45.00 per hour, which pursuant to
  the City Charter, cannot exceed 20 hours per week.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 10 letters advocating for the City
  Council to reconsider the City's Rent Stabilization Department,
  expressing concerns with the actions of the Pasadena Rental
  Housing Board, and providing comments related to the staff report,
  which were all received by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the
  City Council, posted online, and made part of the public record for
  this item.

  Following discussion, on the order of the Vice Mayor, by consensus
  of the City Council, the information was received and filed.
